tagline: A twelve-island ferry grid with 3.5 million visitors, a live daily corridor to Turkey, and almost every hop inside all-electric range.
summary: Rhodes anchors the Dodecanese, the eastern Aegean's island chain running up the Turkish coast — a genuine scheduled-network market where catamarans and fast ferries already stitch Symi, Tilos, Halki, Kos and beyond to Rhodes Town's Mandraki harbour. The grid is dense, weather-exposed and overwhelmingly inside 70 nm legs, making it one of the Mediterranean's cleanest candidates for an all-electric foiling upgrade. A UNESCO-listed medieval harbour city and a cluster of energy-pioneer green islands give the clean-fleet case a ready-made stage.

demand_signals.label: Record tourism volume
demand_signals.value: 3.5M arrivals in 2024 (Jan–Sep) — an all-time record, +12–14% YoY
demand_signals.note: Rhodes is Greece's second-busiest island destination after Crete

demand_signals.label: Live cross-border corridor
demand_signals.value: ~22 scheduled sailings/week Rhodes↔Marmaris (Turkey), up to 3 daily high-speed catamarans in season
demand_signals.note: An established international passenger corridor with CIQ terminals at both ends — ~25 nm, comfortably all-electric range

demand_signals.label: Scheduled island-hop incumbents
demand_signals.value: Dodekanisos Seaways catamarans + Blue Star and SeaJets line-haul serve the whole chain daily in season
demand_signals.note: Decades of adopted fast-ferry habit on exactly the legs a foiling network would fly — modernise the habit, don't create it
demand_signals.source: Dodekanisos Seaways / Blue Star Ferries schedules

demand_signals.label: Day-trip concentration
demand_signals.value: Symi (~23 nm) and Lindos (~26 nm) absorb thousands of Rhodes day-trippers daily in peak season on conventional excursion boats and ferries
demand_signals.note: Short, high-frequency, premium-leaning legs — the canonical foiling day-trip mesh

demand_signals.label: Green-island demo cluster
demand_signals.value: Tilos runs near-energy-autonomous (EU-flagship hybrid station); Halki is Greece's first GR-eco island (solar + e-mobility)
demand_signals.note: Islands already branded on zero-emission transition — a natural proving ground for an all-electric water link
demand_signals.source: GR-eco islands programme, Greek Ministry of Environment & Energy

use_cases.title: Dodecanese scheduled-network upgrade
use_cases.body: Rhodes↔Symi (~23 nm), Rhodes↔Lindos (~26 nm), Rhodes↔Tilos (~38 nm), Rhodes↔Kos (~58 nm): the existing catamaran grid re-flown as quiet, all-electric foiling services, with the N35 Shuttle's 12–15-seat enclosed cabin matching scheduled island-hop loads.

use_cases.title: Cross-border Rhodes↔Marmaris service
use_cases.body: A ~25 nm international corridor with daily catamarans already running through established CIQ terminals — upgraded to a faster, smoother, zero-emission crossing between two of the eastern Med's biggest resort coasts.

use_cases.title: UNESCO harbour day-trips
use_cases.body: Near-silent foiling departures from Mandraki, under the medieval walls, to Symi's amphitheatre harbour and Lindos bay — removing diesel noise and wash from heritage waterfronts that are the region's postcard assets.

use_cases.title: Far-east marquee runs
use_cases.body: Rhodes to Kastellorizo — the easternmost inhabited edge of the EU (~69 nm, at the very edge of all-electric range) — and onward Aegean line-hauls flown on Quanta-LR when margin or distance demands it.

journeys.today: Crowded excursion boats and catamarans, ~50–105 min, pounding into the meltemi chop on the exposed stretch; peak-day sailings sell out.
journeys.with_navier: A ~23 nm foiling flight above the chop — smooth, near-silent arrival into Symi's neoclassical amphitheatre harbour, with frequency the timetable boats can't match.

journeys.today: ~50 min on a hot coastal road plus donkey-path descent, or a 2-hour excursion-boat crawl.
journeys.with_navier: A ~26 nm coastal foiling run direct into Lindos bay beneath the acropolis — under an hour, no road transfer at all.

journeys.today: Daily high-speed catamarans (~60 min) through CIQ at both ends; diesel, schedule-bound, weather-sensitive.
journeys.with_navier: A ~25 nm all-electric international crossing — faster boarding-to-boarding, smooth in the afternoon wind, zero emissions across a binational tourism corridor.

journeys.today: Infrequent subsidised ferry calls or a small ATR flight; the EU's easternmost island feels cut off.
journeys.with_navier: A ~69 nm direct run at the very edge of the all-electric envelope (near range edge — flown with full margin planning, or on Quanta-LR for all-weather schedule reliability).

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Dodecanese is a textbook Pioneer II mesh: Rhodes↔Symi ~23 nm, Rhodes↔Lindos ~26 nm, Symi↔Tilos ~27 nm, Symi↔Halki ~31 nm, Rhodes↔Marmaris ~25 nm, Rhodes↔Kos ~58 nm — virtually the entire scheduled grid inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with D-Marin Kos Marina and Rhodes Marina as natural charging anchors. Faliraki↔Kastellorizo (~69 nm) and Tilos↔Karpathos (~67 nm) sit near the range edge and are flagged for ops-margin confirmation.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (700 nm hybrid, no charging-infrastructure dependency) carries the line-hauls beyond the mesh: Dodecanese↔Cyclades and Dodecanese↔Crete connections, plus all-weather schedule cover on the near-edge legs like Kastellorizo where battery margin is tight.

competitive_landscape: The water network already exists and runs daily: Dodekanisos Seaways catamarans across the island ring, Blue Star and SeaJets on the line-hauls, and high-speed operators on the Rhodes↔Marmaris international corridor. That is the demand evidence — decades of adopted fast-ferry habit. The pain is equally established: diesel catamarans pound in the meltemi, peak sailings sell out, thin winter schedules strand the small islands, and heritage harbours absorb the noise and wash. The upgrade path, not the demand, is the open question.
seasonality: The meltemi blows NW through July–August, building short afternoon chop on the exposed inter-island stretches — the exact conditions where foiling above the waves converts the fleet's roughest, most cancellation-prone days into its showcase. Peak season May–Oct; the civic and lifeline legs (Symi, Tilos, Halki) need year-round service that small conventional boats struggle to hold in winter.
regulatory_note: Greek-flag domestic passenger rules under Hellenic Coast Guard oversight; most island ports sit under the Dodecanese Municipal Port Fund, a single public authority spanning roughly seven harbours — so one agreement can open many ports. Rhodes' Medieval City is UNESCO-listed, making a quiet zero-emission harbour fleet a direct heritage-protection upgrade at Mandraki. The Rhodes↔Marmaris leg runs through established international CIQ terminals; Kastellorizo↔Kaş (~2 nm) is the shortest Greece–Turkey crossing and similarly CIQ-gated.

precedents.why_it_matters: An archipelago-scale scheduled foiling network is already funded and in delivery — the playbook for an island-chain grid like the Dodecanese.

precedents.what: GR-eco islands programme — Halki first flagship
precedents.why_it_matters: The Greek state is already funding zero-emission island transitions inside this exact archipelago; the water link is the missing leg of a live national programme.
